message.content:
No, such discrete variables do not exist.
The reason is basic.
A finite expectation means integrability.
For X this means the positive and negative parts are finite.
For Y the same condition holds.
Let X and Y be discrete random variables.
Assume the expectation of X is finite.
Assume the expectation of Y is finite.
Then X is integrable.
Then Y is integrable.
The sum of the two variables is also integrable.
This follows from the triangle inequality.
The absolute value of the sum is bounded by the sum of absolute values.
Taking expectations preserves the inequality.
The expectation of the absolute value of X is finite.
The expectation of the absolute value of Y is finite.
Therefore the expectation of the absolute value of the sum is finite.
A finite absolute expectation defines a finite expectation.
So the expectation of the sum cannot be undefined.
It cannot be infinite either.
The linearity of expectation applies in this case.
This answers the reference question.
The final point is that no discrete counterexample can give finite expectations for the two marginals while the sum has diverging positive and negative tails and this impossibility in simple form still lies beneath the usual linearity condition.
